blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.

# gh-681: park-reset defeated by silent-update racing the human retrigger push (bot merge buries the human head)

## Description

## Live case

fa #1213, 2026-10-03 22:25–23:10.

1. PR parked `validation_failed` 22:31 (transient red; checks green again by 22:4x).
2. Human (non-machine) pushed a retrigger commit 7ecf11d7 to the branch at ~22:56 — exactly the park-reset contract: human push newer than park should unpark.
3. The bridge/silent-update bot then merged main into the branch (head became bot-merge b3f9c6b5) BEFORE the next real tick.
4. The unpark probe checks **headCommitActor**: head author = machine → probe declines → park persists. Real ticks at 22:59/23:04/23:06 processed the PR 4× without unparking.

Manual recovery: `gh issue edit <pr> --remove-label validation_failed`.

## Fix direction

The probe should not depend on the HEAD being the human commit. Options:
- Walk back past merge commits authored by the machine author (bot merges of main are never the retrigger) to the last substantive commit and test THAT actor + date.
- Or record `parkedAt` vs the branch's last **non-machine-authored** commit timestamp, regardless of ordering.

## Impact

Every parked guest PR whose branch gets silent-updated (BEHIND heads — common) can never auto-unpark on the owner's fix push. Same freeze class the original park-reset (#668) killed.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

Shallow history (1 commit). Let me look at the current implementation more carefully, then design the fix.

Current probe order in the `update_branch` localAction:

1. fail closed if any probe failed
2. `headChangedNoVerdictVf` — head sha changed from the parked sha AND the new head has no red verdict of its own → clear (the #633 fix)
3. `machinePushVf` — head moved by the machine → hold
4. `!freshPushVf` — head predates the park → hold
5. else → clear (human push newer than park)

The live case fa#1213 (gh-681):
- Parked 22:31, parked-head = sha A.
- Human pushes 7ecf11d7 (~22:56): head changes to a human commit — but no tick ran before the bot merge.
- Bot merges main → head = b3f9c6b5 (committer sm-silent-update).
- Tick at 22:59: probe sees machine head → holds.

Why doesn't `headChangedNoVerdictVf` fire at 22:59? Conditions:
- parkedHeadVf = sha A (from park comment), uHead = b3f9c6b5 → differ ✓
- `latestDispatchedVerdict(repo, workflow, b3f9c6b5) !== 'failure'` — must be true to clear.

Hmm wait. Actually — hold on. Let me re-read the ticket again:

"The unpark probe checks headCommitActor: head author = machine → probe declines → park persists."

Hmm, so the probe that declined is the headCommitActor-based check. Let me check: maybe in the deployed version at the time, the order was different — machinePushVf checked BEFORE headChangedNoVerdictVf. The #633 fix comment says "owner 2026-10-02" and the live case is 2026-10-03... 

Hmm, wait — actually let me reconsider. Maybe there's a subtlety: in the live case the checks "green again by 22:4x". Maybe the CI at fa is dispatch-based, and someone/something re-dispatched... "transient red" suggests a check failed then went green — maybe via re-run of a foreign (push-based) CI. So there could be workflow runs on the branch heads.

Actually — hmm, one more consideration. What if there WAS a red verdict on the bot-merge head? No wait — the bot merge push doesn't fire CI (PAT push), and the parked PR gets no dispatches.

OK let me take yet another angle: maybe the deployed fa deployment had the pre-#633 code for this live case, and the ticket (gh-681) is being filed now against this repo, where #633 IS present. So the question for me: does the current code still have the gh-681 bug?

Tick at 22:59, PR has label validation_failed:

- lastCommitter = gh api commits/b3f9c6b5 --jq '.committer.name' → 'sm-silent-update'
- actorVf = {login: .author.login // .committer.login, date: .committer.date}. The merge commit was created by git on the runner with `-c user.name=sm-silent-update -c user.email=sm-silent-update@users.noreply.github.com`, pushed via a token URL. GitHub maps the commit's author/committer email to accounts if linked. sm-silent-update@users.noreply.github.com is probably NOT linked → author.login and committer.login are null → login = ''. Or the deployment's machineAuthor login could carry it. Ticket says "head author = machine".
- parkedAtVf = 22:31 event.
- machineLoginVf = machine author login (e.g. 'ai-teammate-bot').
- machinePushVf = lastCommitter === 'sm-silent-update' → TRUE.
- freshPushVf = merge date (22:57) > 22:31 → true (irrelevant).

- headChangedNoVerdictVf = uHead !== sha A && latestDispatchedVerdict(b3f9c6b5) !== 'failure'.

Now the question: what does latestDispatchedVerdict return for b3f9c6b5 in the live case? If null → clear happens → bug fixed already by #633? If 'failure' → hold persists.

Hmm, wait. Hmm, "checks green again by 22:4x" — this suggests the PR's checks rollup went green. On which sha? The 22:31 head (sha A). Transient red — e.g., a flaky check re-run green.

But what fired CI at 22:31 if CI is dispatch-only? "Real ticks at 22:59/23:04/23:06 processed the PR 4×" — hmm, and the park comment says "no validation CI is dispatched for it".

Hmm, unless the fa deployment has push-based CI for external contributors... Actually the fa deployment — the guests push to branches, and there IS a CI that runs (validation_failed implies checks exist and were red). The comment in code says "Validation trigger (dispatch-only CI): no push ever fires CI on its own — the SM is the only trigger." for the repos the SM manages. But a "GUEST PR" (external contributor PR)... the parked one at fa#923 was a guest PR with red checks.

OK you know what — I'm going around in circles speculating about the live case's exact probe outputs. The important thing: the ticket asks for the fix direction explicitly:

> ## Fix direction
> The probe should not depend on the HEAD being the human commit. Options:
> - Walk back past merge commits authored by the machine author (bot merges of main are never the retrigger) to the last substantive commit and test THAT actor + date.
> - Or record `parkedAt` vs the branch's last **non-machine-authored** commit timestamp, regardless of ordering.

So the fix: when the head was moved by the machine (bot merge), walk back through the commit history past machine-authored commits to the last substantive (non-machine-authored) commit, and test THAT commit's actor + date against the park. This way:
- Live case: head b3f9c6b5 (machine) → walk back past it → 7ecf11d7 (human, 22:56) → actor = human, date > park (22:31) → UNPARK. ✓

- Machine agent-leg push (rework auto-save by ai-teammate login): walk back past machine commits → last human commit → if that's older than the park → hold. ✓ (Machine movement never clears.)
- Human retrigger push, no bot merge: head = 7ecf11d7 (human) directly → existing path works.
- New: what about a human push that is a MERGE? E.g. human merges main into their branch via GitHub UI (author = human). Then head is a merge commit authored by the human — fine, walk-back stops there; actor = human, date newer → unpark. Good.

Also need to keep the #633 head-changed clear working (it fires before, and when it fires, unpark happens anyway).

Now, why didn't #633 clear the fa#1213 park? Let me think ONE more time... 

OH WAIT. I see it now! Look at the `headChangedNoVerdictVf` condition again:

Probe error → null → `null !== 'failure'` → true → CLEAR?! That contradicts the comment... wait:

- probe error → latestDispatchedVerdict catches → returns null → `null !== 'failure'` → true → headChangedNoVerdictVf true → CLEAR. That's fail OPEN, contradicting the comment "probe error keeps the park".

Hmm, but that's a different concern. The intent: probe error → null → keeps the park. But the code `!== 'failure'` with null makes it clear. Hmm — that looks like a BUG in the #633 fix (fail-open instead of fail-closed)... but not our ticket. Hmm. Actually wait, maybe not: if the probe errors, `latestDispatchedVerdict` logs 'verdict probe failed' and returns null → headChangedNoVerdictVf = true → unpark. The comment says probe error should keep the park. So there's a discrepancy. But not gh-681's core.

Hmm hold on, actually, let me reconsider — maybe THAT's not relevant. Let me refocus on gh-681's live case: why did the park persist at fa#1213 on 2026-10-03 if #633 (2026-10-02) was deployed?

## Plan (TDD)

### RED: Write failing tests first in `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`, extending the sticky-park suite (after the #633 tests, before the validate_pr tests).

Fixture additions:
- `PARKED_HEAD = '1111223333444455666677778899990000'` (the sha at park time) — actually for these tests I'll omit prComments so `parkedHeadSha` returns '' → headChangedNoVerdictVf false → the machine branch is reached. This also proves the walk-back doesn't depend on comment bookkeeping.
- `BOT_HEAD = 'b3f9c6b5...'` full 40-hex, `RETRIG = '7ecf11d7...'` 40-hex.
- A `vfCommits(list)` stub builder: intercepts `/commits?sha=` → JSON.stringify(list); otherwise delegate to `vfCli({...})`.

Careful with the existing vfCli regex: `/\/commits\/([0-9a-fA-Z]+)"/` — my walk-back command is `gh api "repos/a/b/commits?sha=BOT&per_page=30"` — contains `/commits?sha=` — no `/commits/<sha>"` match. And the events probe: my command has no `/events?per_page=100`. Good, no interference. But note the ORDER inside vfCli — irrelevant for non-matching commands.

Tests:

**T1 (gh-681 live case — clears):** 
- item 213: labels ['validation_failed'], headSha: BOT_HEAD, branch feat/vf-213.
- committers: BOT_HEAD → 'sm-silent-update'; actors: BOT_HEAD → {login: '', date: '2026-10-03T22:57:00Z'} (bot merge actor unmapped; hmm — login '' → machinePushVf via committer name only ✓; also make the head date FRESH (22:57 > park 22:31) to prove it's not the freshness of the HEAD that matters but the substantive commit).

  Hmm wait, actually more faithful to the live case: actor login = machine ('ai-teammate')? The ticket says "head author = machine". Set actors: BOT_HEAD → {login: 'ai-teammate', date: '2026-10-03T22:57:00Z'}. Then machinePushVf true via BOTH committer name and login. And even though the head date is fresh, the head is machine — old code held here... well, old-old code held; the current code would hit #633 first if prComments present — I OMIT prComments so #633 can't rescue: parkedHeadVf = '' → headChangedNoVerdictVf false. THIS is the remaining-freeze scenario that exists in the CURRENT code (park comment missing/deleted/legacy → permanent freeze). 
- commits stub: [BOT_HEAD (committer name sm-silent-update, login null, date 22:57, parents [RETRIG]), RETRIG (author/committer login 'guest-human', name 'real-dev', committer date '2026-10-03T22:56:00Z', parents [PARKED_SHA])]
- parkedAt: '2026-10-03T22:31:00Z' → RETRIG 22:56 > 22:31 → CLEAR.
- assert: capturedPrLabelRemoves has validation_failed; capturedPrComments[0].body contains 'buried' and RETRIG prefix (7ecf11d7) and 'guest-human'; refresh still ran.

**T2 (substantive commit is human but OLDER than the park — holds):**
- item 214, BOT_HEAD committer sm-silent-update, actor machine fresh; commits stub: [BOT_HEAD (sm-silent-update, parents [OLD_HUMAN]), OLD_HUMAN ('real-dev', date '2026-10-03T22:20:00Z' < park 22:31)]
- assert: no label remove, no comment.

**T3 (only machine commits in the walk — holds):**
- item 215, head BOT_HEAD2 (sm-silent-update committer, machine login), commits: [BOT_HEAD2 (sm-silent-update, parents [BOT_HEAD1]), BOT_HEAD1 (sm-silent-update, parents [])] → walk exhausts → hold.
- assert: no label remove, no comment. (machine-login variant: make BOT_HEAD1 actor login ai-teammate to exercise the login branch of isMachine.)

**T4 (walk probe dead — fail closed, holds):**
- item 216, machine head; the `/commits?sha=` stub returns '' (garbage) → probe gets no list → null → hold.
- assert: no label remove, no comment. (This also pins "walk window miss → hold".)

Also worth: **T5 (bot merge whose merged-in MAIN human commit must NOT count — first-parent discipline):** head BOT_HEAD (machine), main contributed a FRESH human commit MAIN_C (date after park) that appears in the plain list AFTER... hmm, in the plain list, main's commits DO appear (ancestors via 2nd parent). My walk follows parents[0] — from BOT_HEAD parents[0] = RETRIG (branch history) — main commits are skipped even though present in the list. To test this: commits list = [BOT_HEAD (machine, parents: [{sha: RETRIG}, {sha: MAIN_C}]), RETRIG (human STALE 22:20 < park), MAIN_C (human FRESH 22:58 — merged in from main!), ...]. Walk: BOT_HEAD machine → parents[0] = RETRIG → human but STALE → hold (must NOT jump to MAIN_C fresh). Without first-parent discipline the walk would find MAIN_C fresh → wrongly clear. Great test of the subtle part.

### GREEN: implement

1. Add `lastSubstantiveCommitActor(repoInfo, headSha, machineLogin)` function near `parkedHeadSha` (after it, ~line 2620).
2. Wire into the update_branch park block: inside `else if (machinePushVf) {` — compute substantive, new sub-branch clear, else hold.

Wait — careful about the CURRENT chain shape:

```js
if (lastCommitter === null || actorVf === null || parkedAtVf === null) {
    fail-closed hold
} else if (headChangedNoVerdictVf) {
    clear (sha change)
} else if (machinePushVf) {
    hold log
} else if (!freshPushVf) {
    hold log
} else {
    clear (human push)
}
```

New:

```js
} else if (machinePushVf) {
    var substantiveVf = lastSubstantiveCommitActor(effectiveRepoInfo, uHead, machineLoginVf);
    var substantiveFreshVf = !!(substantiveVf && substantiveVf.date && parkedAtVf &&
        Date.parse(substantiveVf.date) > Date.parse(parkedAtVf));
    if (substantiveFreshVf) {
        clear (buried retrigger)
    } else {
        hold log (existing message)
    }
```

`var` in block — function-scoped, fine for GraalJS. But redeclaration across loop iterations: `var substantiveVf` inside the per-item loop body — hoists to the tick function; re-assigned per iteration before use. Safe.

Hmm — one concern: `var` declared inside an `else if` block that may never execute; if another iteration's path READS substantiveVf before assignment... my code only reads it right after assigning in the same block. Safe.

3. Also — should the walk-back run when `machinePushVf` is true but uHead is null? uHead null → lastCommitter null → fail-closed earlier. Safe: machinePushVf implies lastCommitter !== 'sm...' — wait no: machinePushVf = lastCommitter === 'sm-silent-update' || login match — if lastCommitter is null → fail-closed branch already caught it. In the machinePushVf branch, uHead must be non-null (lastCommitter non-null requires uHead non-null; login-match requires actorVf non-null which requires uHead). So no extra guard needed, but cheap `uHead &&` guard anyway inside the call condition — I'll pass uHead directly; it's guaranteed non-null there. Keep code simple.

Comment/log wording — match house style with incident reference:

# gh-681: park-reset defeated by silent-update racing the human retrigger push (bot merge buries the human head)

## Description

## Live case

fa #1213, 2026-10-03 22:25–23:10.

1. PR parked `validation_failed` 22:31 (transient red; checks green again by 22:4x).
2. Human (non-machine) pushed a retrigger commit 7ecf11d7 to the branch at ~22:56 — exactly the park-reset contract: human push newer than park should unpark.
3. The bridge/silent-update bot then merged main into the branch (head became bot-merge b3f9c6b5) BEFORE the next real tick.
4. The unpark probe checks **headCommitActor**: head author = machine → probe declines → park persists. Real ticks at 22:59/23:04/23:06 processed the PR 4× without unparking.

Manual recovery: `gh issue edit <pr> --remove-label validation_failed`.

## Fix direction

The probe should not depend on the HEAD being the human commit. Options:
- Walk back past merge commits authored by the machine author (bot merges of main are never the retrigger) to the last substantive commit and test THAT actor + date.
- Or record `parkedAt` vs the branch's last **non-machine-authored** commit timestamp, regardless of ordering.

## Impact

Every parked guest PR whose branch gets silent-updated (BEHIND heads — common) can never auto-unpark on the owner's fix push. Same freeze class the original park-reset (#668) killed.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# gh-681: park-reset defeated by silent-update racing the human retrigger push (bot merge buries the human head)

## Description

## Live case

fa #1213, 2026-10-03 22:25–23:10.

1. PR parked `validation_failed` 22:31 (transient red; checks green again by 22:4x).
2. Human (non-machine) pushed a retrigger commit 7ecf11d7 to the branch at ~22:56 — exactly the park-reset contract: human push newer than park should unpark.
3. The bridge/silent-update bot then merged main into the branch (head became bot-merge b3f9c6b5) BEFORE the next real tick.
4. The unpark probe checks **headCommitActor**: head author = machine → probe declines → park persists. Real ticks at 22:59/23:04/23:06 processed the PR 4× without unparking.

Manual recovery: `gh issue edit <pr> --remove-label validation_failed`.

## Fix direction

The probe should not depend on the HEAD being the human commit. Options:
- Walk back past merge commits authored by the machine author (bot merges of main are never the retrigger) to the last substantive commit and test THAT actor + date.
- Or record `parkedAt` vs the branch's last **non-machine-authored** commit timestamp, regardless of ordering.

## Impact

Every parked guest PR whose branch gets silent-updated (BEHIND heads — common) can never auto-unpark on the owner's fix push. Same freeze class the original park-reset (#668) killed.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

arguments.content:
### What changed The `validation_failed` unpark probe no longer depends on the HEAD commit being human: when the head was moved by the machine (silent-update bot merge / agent auto-save), it now walks back past machine commits on the branch's first-parent chain to the last substantive commit and tests THAT actor + date against the park event — so a human retrigger buried under a bot merge unparks instead of freezing forever (live fa#1213: park held through 4 ticks). ### Key decisions - New `lastSubstantiveCommitActor` probe in `js/smAgent.js` (single `gh api` ancestor-list call, walk capped at 30); fail-closed like the other park probes (dead probe / all-machine chain → park holds). - **First-parent walk only**: the plain ancestor list interleaves main's history, so a fresh human commit on main (merged in *by* the bot) must not read as this branch's retrigger — pinned by a dedicated test. - Machine detection matches the existing contract: `sm-silent-update` committer identity OR the deployment's machineAuthor login on author/committer; machine movement alone still never clears the park. - Existing reset paths untouched: head-sha change with no own verdict (#633) still fires first; docs (`docs/agents/sm_github.md` + generated) updated to the new contract. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json # 219 passed — 5 new tests incl. the fa#1213 burial replay dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # 1360 passed, 0 failed ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD TICK[SM tick, PR parked validation_failed] --> HEAD{head actor machine?} HEAD -->|no| OLD[existing human-push newer-than-park check] HEAD -->|yes| WALK[lastSubstantiveCommitActor
first-parent walk past machine commits] WALK -->|human commit newer than park| UNPARK[remove label + comment + re-validate] WALK -->|stale / all-machine / probe error| HOLD[park holds] ```

# gh-681: park-reset defeated by silent-update racing the human retrigger push (bot merge buries the human head)

## Description

## Live case

fa #1213, 2026-10-03 22:25–23:10.

1. PR parked `validation_failed` 22:31 (transient red; checks green again by 22:4x).
2. Human (non-machine) pushed a retrigger commit 7ecf11d7 to the branch at ~22:56 — exactly the park-reset contract: human push newer than park should unpark.
3. The bridge/silent-update bot then merged main into the branch (head became bot-merge b3f9c6b5) BEFORE the next real tick.
4. The unpark probe checks **headCommitActor**: head author = machine → probe declines → park persists. Real ticks at 22:59/23:04/23:06 processed the PR 4× without unparking.

Manual recovery: `gh issue edit <pr> --remove-label validation_failed`.

## Fix direction

The probe should not depend on the HEAD being the human commit. Options:
- Walk back past merge commits authored by the machine author (bot merges of main are never the retrigger) to the last substantive commit and test THAT actor + date.
- Or record `parkedAt` vs the branch's last **non-machine-authored** commit timestamp, regardless of ordering.

## Impact

Every parked guest PR whose branch gets silent-updated (BEHIND heads — common) can never auto-unpark on the owner's fix push. Same freeze class the original park-reset (#668) killed.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# gh-681: park-reset defeated by silent-update racing the human retrigger push (bot merge buries the human head)

## Description

## Live case

fa #1213, 2026-10-03 22:25–23:10.

1. PR parked `validation_failed` 22:31 (transient red; checks green again by 22:4x).
2. Human (non-machine) pushed a retrigger commit 7ecf11d7 to the branch at ~22:56 — exactly the park-reset contract: human push newer than park should unpark.
3. The bridge/silent-update bot then merged main into the branch (head became bot-merge b3f9c6b5) BEFORE the next real tick.
4. The unpark probe checks **headCommitActor**: head author = machine → probe declines → park persists. Real ticks at 22:59/23:04/23:06 processed the PR 4× without unparking.

Manual recovery: `gh issue edit <pr> --remove-label validation_failed`.

## Fix direction

The probe should not depend on the HEAD being the human commit. Options:
- Walk back past merge commits authored by the machine author (bot merges of main are never the retrigger) to the last substantive commit and test THAT actor + date.
- Or record `parkedAt` vs the branch's last **non-machine-authored** commit timestamp, regardless of ordering.

## Impact

Every parked guest PR whose branch gets silent-updated (BEHIND heads — common) can never auto-unpark on the owner's fix push. Same freeze class the original park-reset (#668) killed.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

You help with software engineering tasks in the working directory /home/runner/work/dmtools-agents/dmtools-agents. ## Agent messaging

You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a10406-c87f-7352-9a49-fbcd467fa106/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender's address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.
When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project's file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).

Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host's config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.

## The owner talks to you only

The owner's messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner's address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child's result lands, report it back.
